text:
Aisha: Weird one — I ran `rlw login` (our CLI) to get an ephemeral session token for local dev, then started the sampleapp with `npm run dev`. Background worker that spawns a child process to call embeddings got 403s. Main process calls succeeded. Anyone seen env not propagating to child procs?

Tom: Are you on mac/linux or Windows? Windows has different env inheritance semantics. Also how does rlw login export the token? Does it print `export REDWOOD_SESSION_TOKEN=...` or write to disk?

Aisha: macOS. rlw login uses the OS keyring and also optionally writes a `~/.config/redwood/session.json` when you pass `--persist`. I didn't pass --persist, so only keyring was populated. Parent process can read via our native keyring call, but the child is a plain bash script that expects REDWOOD_SESSION_TOKEN env var.

Priya: Ah — that combo explains it. Child bash scripts only see env at spawn time. If parent reads token at runtime (via keyring) and doesn't set process.env before spawning, the child won't inherit it. We need clearer docs or a helper that injects envs for subprocesses.

Leo: Another angle: we have two token types — long-lived API keys (REDWOOD_API_KEY) and ephemeral session tokens (REDWOOD_SESSION_TOKEN). Sampleapps mix both patterns. Some examples spawn `child_process.exec('node worker.js')` without passing env: `{ env: process.env }` so if you set process.env after spawn, child misses it.

Aisha: Exactly. I patched the sampleapp worker to use a spawn wrapper that ensures env is set before spawn. Quick patch: `const env = Object.assign({}, process.env, { REDWOOD_SESSION_TOKEN: await getSessionToken() }); spawn('node', ['worker.js'], { env })`. But that's manual and brittle.

Tom: For DX, two improvements: 1) CLI should support `--export` that prints shell-friendly exports so users can `eval $(rlw login --export)`; 2) SDKs should have a small credential helper that spawns child procs with injected env when you intentionally start background jobs.

Priya: I propose we standardize a credential lookup file path for ephemeral sessions: `~/.config/redwood/active_session` with strict permissions. SDKs can read that file synchronously at process start and before any spawn and optionally watch it for changes. This would be cross-platform and avoid forcing keyring deps in simple sampleapps.

Leo: Can we avoid polling? Maybe a file-based lock notification or FS watch for linux/mac and fallback poll on windows. Also document fallbacks: env var > session file > keyring > explicit constructor apiKey.

Aisha: Parity request: Go SDK doesn't read the keyring by default but looks at REDWOOD_API_KEY only. Node and Python do a lot of heuristics. We need a consistent precedence matrix across SDKs.

Tom: Proposed precedence: 1) explicit credentials in constructor, 2) REDWOOD_API_KEY (long-lived), 3) REDWOOD_SESSION_TOKEN (ephemeral env), 4) ~/.config/redwood/active_session (file), 5) OS keyring credential helper, 6) CLI credential helper via `rlw credentials` (interactive). Document this and signal incompatible behavior in sampleapps.

Priya: For rotation: when a session token refreshes, background workers should get a SIGHUP-based callback to pick up new creds, or the SDK should expose `onCredentialChanged` hook so apps can rehydrate child environments.

Leo: Small nit: we should avoid creating more env names. Let's map `REDWOOD_SESSION_TOKEN` as the canonical ephemeral name and deprecate `REDWOOD_TOKEN` found in older samples. I'll grep the repo and open a cleanup PR.

devex-bot: Created ticket RED-3577: "CLI/session UX: export flag, active_session file, SDK precedence + child-process credential helper" and linked checklist template.

Aisha: Action items: Tom -> add `--export` to `rlw login` and docs; Priya -> spec active_session file and watcher strategy; Leo -> repo grep and samples cleanup PR; SDK owners -> align precedence and add child-spawn helper API. I'll add to the devex backlog and tag owners. Thanks!

Tom: One more: update onboarding doc so new hires running sampleapps don't have to `--persist` or touch keyring. Make the file path the recommended quickstart for ephemeral local runs.

Priya: I'll draft the doc blurb and throw it in the sampleapps README. Expect a draft by EOD. :white_check_mark:
